title: Priority ladder & curated intake for hosted chat + streaming + tool calls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a repeatable, scoring-driven intake and prioritization process (a "priority ladder") for Hosted API feature requests focused on chat, streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs from enterprise customers. The ladder will produce a ranked queue and a gating checklist for Dedicated/Private escalation, including suggested guardrails (rate limits, fallback models, structured-output validators) and a recommended SLA band. Goal is to reduce ad-hoc request handling, accelerate high-value enterprise approvals, and codify trade-offs between latency/cost and data residency/compliance.
acceptance_criteria: A documented priority ladder scoring rubric that can be applied to new requests within 48 hours

An intake form template (Confluence + support intake link) capturing signals for automatic scoring: customer size, regulatory constraints, throughput targets, latency SLO, data residency, uptime SLA, model-specific needs
A gating checklist for Dedicated/Private escalation with explicit security/KMS and audit log requirements
A recommended default rollback & fallback policy for streaming/tool-call failures (model variant + region fallback + circuit-breaker thresholds)
Pilot with 3 recent enterprise requests applied retrospectively and feedback collected from Solutions Eng and Sales
tasks: Draft scoring rubric: weightings for customer revenue tier, SLA ask, regulatory constraints, complexity of toolchain (tool calls / external integrations), and expected query volume
Prototype intake form in Confluence and a short web intake (support) template
Work session with Solutions Eng and Sales to validate rubric and gather edge-case signals (2 hours)
Define default tech guardrails: streaming timeout, fallback model variants, structured-output schema validation approach
Document handoff & escalation path to ENG and Security (+ PR template for implementation proposals)
comments: 2025-02-20 Aisha: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded to Confluence - link below. Initial rubric draft attached. Priority: accelerate decision time for enterprise asks.
2025-02-22 Marco: Pulled three recent intake tickets for retrospective scoring. Two would have been P0 under this rubric; one would be P2. Need to discuss SLA bands for mid-market customers.
2025-02-24 Elena (Solutions Eng): Concern about requiring KMS for all Private escalations; suggested 'KMS required for regulated PII/PHI only' and provide alternative guidance for non-sensitive data.

2025-02-25 Priya (Security): Quick review - gated checklist looks good. Request adding a field for 'data retention policy' and adding a flag for 'third-party tool calls' to trigger threat-model review.

2025-02-27 Marco: Added fallback policy draft. Proposed: region fallback first, then model-variant fallback; streaming circuit-breaker at 4% error rate over 5 minutes or sustained latency >2x SLO for 3 minutes.

2025-02-28 Aisha: Ready for PM leadership review. Updated acceptance criteria and examples of scored requests included. Requesting decision on whether cost impact threshold should be explicit in rubric (suggested threshold: >20% expected per-token cost increase -> bump priority by 1).
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: stricter gating (KMS + audit log required) speeds compliance but may slow onboarding of non-regulated customers. Decided to make KMS mandatory only for PII/PHI or when customer requests Private deployment.

Tradeoff: aggressive fallback (always route to cheaper quantized variant) reduces cost but can regress quality. We prefer semantic-preserving fallback order (region -> model variant with explicit quality label -> scaled-down batch size) and require a regression test set for each fallback family.
Operational decision: Solutions Eng will own first-pass scoring for inbound enterprise requests; PM will audit weekly and propose adjustments to weights.
Unresolved: exact numeric weights for 'expected delta in per-token cost' and whether it should be additive or multiplicative to the final score. Follow-up in next cycle.
implementation_notes: Suggested tooling: add a simple scoring calculator sheet and automations to tag Linear tickets with initial score
Implementation owners: PM -> intake form + rubric; Solutions Eng -> validation and pilot; ENG -> provide fallback implementation proposals and define monitoring metrics

Metrics to track post-launch: median time from intake to decision, % of requests escalated to Dedicated/Private, SLA breach rate for escalated features, false-positive gating (denials that later should have been approved)
